title: post-upgrade-nodeagent-init-race-and-manifest-drift-remediation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
During several Private/VPC customer upgrades we observed an intermittent post-upgrade failure that left clusters in a degraded state: nodeagent pods repeatedly restarted and the operator reconciler overwrote customer config with stale generated manifests, producing a persistent config drift. This ticket tracks the triage, patching, and rollout for a targeted remediation and safe hotfix release.

Background and scope:
- Affected product: Redwood Private (on-prem/VPC).
- Symptoms reported by 3 customers during upgrades in the last 2 weeks: repeated nodeagent crashloop, HelmRelease stuck in post-upgrade phase, operator reconcilers planting older manifests into the cluster leading to feature flags and K8s RBAC being reverted.
- Reproducibility: intermittent at scale, reliably reproduced in our internal staging by forcing Helm hook concurrency and introducing a slow secret write on nodeagent initialization.

Root cause (summary):
- Helm chart contains init hooks and post-upgrade hooks for nodeagent + operator components that could execute concurrently across multiple controller-manager replicas.
- Nodeagent startup writes an opaque config Secret used by the operator to compute projected manifests. A timing window exists where operator reads the absence of the secret and synthesizes a default manifest; later the nodeagent writes the secret but the operator's reconciliation loop applies its older default manifest (timestamp-based merge) and overwrites the later secret/ConfigMap, causing config drift.
- The Helm hooks ordering relied on Kubernetes hook weight heuristics but did not handle controller failover and multi-replica races, making the issue intermittent across clusters.

Impact and customer escalations:
- Impact: customer workloads experienced degraded inference capacity and, in one case, failed failover of Dedicated-to-Private replication during upgrade. Several customers opened high-severity tickets; two escalations to enterprise support required Live Eng involvement.
- Known customers: AcmeHealth (escalated), FinLogic (escalated), AtlasRetail (monitoring).

Investigation artifacts and links:
- Repro harness (staging): https://github.com/redwood-inference/onprem-staging/tree/upgrade-race-harness
- Incident channel: #inc-upgrades (log thread pinned) https://slack.redwood.com/inc-upgrades-thread-3412
- Customer error traces and kube-logs attached in incident thread and drive: https://drive.redwood.com/incident/ENG-88321-artifacts

Proposed remediation plan (phased):
1) Short term emergency patch (hotfix):
   - Add a deterministic Helm hook sequencing: convert nodeagent init to a pre-install/pre-upgrade "pre-hook" with explicit hook-weight and a blocking readiness probe; introduce a post-install barrier job that waits for the nodeagent config secret to exist before allowing operator post-upgrade hooks to run.
   - Modify operator reconciler to perform a conservative merge: prefer newer secrets/configmaps when resourceVersion/timestamp indicates later write; avoid blind overwrites of user-provided keys.
   - Release a hotpatch operator chart: operator-chart v0.3.7-hotfix1 and nodeagent v1.12.4-hotfix.
   - Goal: eliminate the race window and prevent destructive overwrites.

2) Medium term follow-up (1-2 sprints):
   - Add preflight validation to the onprem upgrade controller that performs a dry-run check for missing secrets and validates hook ordering.
   - Enhance reconciler to do schema-aware diffs and a three-way merge against last-applied-configuration to avoid future regressions.
   - Add automated e2e upgrade tests that introduce artificial latency to startup and validate idempotency.

3) Long term (Q3):
   - Operator-level leader election improvements to serialize sensitive upgrade steps across replicas.
   - Surface hook sequencing/upgrade health indicators in Console so customers get early warning before a problematic upgrade.

Rollout strategy:
- Staged rollout: internal staging -> canary customers (non-critical) -> opt-in enterprise customers -> forced policy for all upgrades after monitoring window.
- Rollback plan: HelmChart maintain previous revision channel operator-chart v0.3.6; automated rollback via upgrade-controller if healthchecks fail for >10 minutes across canary clusters.
- Monitoring: Add Prometheus alert for reconcilers that perform >3 overwrites to the same secret within 5m and a Console dashboard tile for upgrade health.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We prefer a non-breaking operator code change that uses conservative merging rather than immediate deletion of synthesised manifests. This increases code complexity but avoids data loss for customers.
- Using a blocking pre-upgrade barrier job increases upgrade latency slightly for large clusters but reduces risk; customers will be notified in release notes.
- Backward compatibility: nodeagent hotfix maintains previous config schema; operator merger will treat unknown fields permissively.

Testing and validation:
- e2e reproduction harness added to CI with a "slow-secret-writer" scenario.
- Unit tests for merge strategy and behavior under resourceVersion skews.
- Manual validation with three customer clusters (AcmeHealth staging, FinLogic preprod, internal-large).

Docs and runbooks:
- Runbook for triage and rollback: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Upgrade-Race-Runbook-ENG-88321
- Customer communication draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/ENG-88321-customer-communication

Next steps (short term):
- PRs open for review (see attachments).
- Prepare hotfix release notes and change-log.
- Schedule canary window with AcmeHealth for 2026-03-16.

Expected outcome:
- Minimize customer downtime and stop destructive config overwrites during upgrades.
- Reduce the frequency of upgrade-related escalations and give engineering time to deliver the medium-term reconciler improvements.
